case_title: L. Krishna Reddy v. State by Station House Officer & Ors.
accused_victim_relationship: Relative (parents-in-law of the victim, the husband's parents)
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 r/w s.34; IPC s.498A r/w s.34
evidence_type: Statements under s.161 Cr.P.C. of several witnesses and the complainant's further statement; no direct evidence against the parents-in-law discussed
trial_court_outcome: Refused discharge of the parents-in-law; proceedings to continue to trial
high_court_outcome: Criminal revision allowed; parents-in-law discharged (order dated 18.10.2011, Crl. R.C. No. 761 of 2010)
neutral_facts: The victim, a married woman, was found dead on 26.3.2006 in a hotel room in Puducherry that had been rented by her husband. Her body bore several stab wounds, and the investigation recorded that she had received 11 injuries from a knife. The investigation placed the incident on the evening of 25.3.2006 at about 19.00 hours in that hotel room. The couple had lived apart from the husband's parents, having set up their own separate residence about six months before the death. The victim's husband later died by suicide by hanging, and a separate case was registered in respect of that death. The investigation concluded that the victim's husband, together with his parents, had subjected her to cruelty over a dowry demand and had caused her death. The complainant, the victim's father, said by telephone that the couple had left Hyderabad for Vijayawada. In his further statement he alleged that the parents had planned the killing with the husband because of dowry harassment. The statements of several witnesses recorded during the investigation did not attribute any direct dowry demand to the parents. The parents were not present in Puducherry when the killing took place.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from multiple stab wounds (11 injuries alleged)
premeditation_planning: Not found by the Court against the parents-in-law; planning was alleged by the complainant only
motive: alleged: dowry harassment (the Court noted no direct imputation of dowry demand against the parents-in-law)
key_evidence_accepted: Absence of any direct imputation in witness statements against the parents-in-law; the complainant's sole conspiracy allegation was a bald statement
witness_credibility: Complainant's statements were described as those of an anguished father; the Court did not find the conspiracy allegation sufficient without further linking evidence
post_offence_conduct: Husband committed suicide shortly after the incident, possibly from guilt and remorse; no post-offence conduct of the parents-in-law noted
trial_duration: offence: 25.3.2006; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 18.10.2011; Supreme Court: 24.10.2013
legal_representation: Appellant (complainant): D. Rama Krishna Reddy, D. Bharathi Reddy; Respondents (accused parents-in-law): Altaf Ahmed, P. Venkat Reddy, Anil Kumar Tandale. No separate State counsel named.
investigation_status: FIR/crime registered 26.3.2006; charge sheet filed 31.5.2007; separate s.174 Cr.P.C. case for husband's suicide registered 24.9.2006
procedural_irregularity: Trial court was noted to have been influenced by a High Court direction to dispose of the case within two months
appeal_history: Trial court: discharge refused. High Court: revision allowed, parents-in-law discharged. Supreme Court: complainant's appeal dismissed.
prosecution_argument: Complainant relied on Stree Atyachar Virodhi Parishad and K. Narayana Rao to urge that the parents-in-law be tried; the Court found these did not support continuing the prosecution
defence_argument: Parents-in-law sought discharge under s.227 Cr.P.C., contending no direct involvement or conspiracy was shown in the charge sheet
legal_principle_applied: Prima facie test under s.227 Cr.P.C.; a bald allegation of conspiracy requires further linking evidence; conspiracy requires an agreement existing at the material time; prosecution that is an exercise in futility should be ended
precedent_relied_upon: Union of India v. Prafulla Kumar Samal (1979) 3 SCC 4; Central Bureau of Investigation v. K. Narayana Rao (2012) 9 SCC 512; State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335; Stree Atyachar Virodhi Parishad v. Dilip Nathumal Chordia (1989) 1 SCC 715
